title: Stack buffer overflow via unbounded memcpy in parse_bravo
rationale: Root cause: entry.c:40 -- memcpy(name, buf, len) copies a caller-controlled length (up to 4095) into a 16-byte stack buffer with no bounds check. The fix clamps len to sizeof(name) - 1 (15) before the copy.
variants_checked: entry.c:parse_alpha -- same unchecked-memcpy pattern (line 27, heap target). Separate finding (f001). entry.c:parse_charlie -- no memcpy, not applicable.
bypass_considered: An attacker supplies exactly 16 bytes of payload (len=15 after the dispatcher subtracts 1). After the clamp, 15 == sizeof(name) - 1, so the condition is false and len stays 15. memcpy writes bytes 0-14, then name[15] is set to '\0'. No overflow.
test_note: No regression test added. The canary target has no C test infrastructure.
review_reason: The single hunk is scoped entirely to parse_bravo, the function containing the bug at entry.c:40. It fixes the root cause by clamping len to sizeof(name) - 1 before the memcpy, preventing the unbounded stack write. No new parsing, trust boundaries, or validation removals are introduced. The idiom is standard C and correctly preserves the existing null-termination at line 41.
